_comment: Declarative catalogue of the firmware images this project analyses.
Vendor firmware is NOT redistributed in this repository. This file plus
tools/fetch-firmware.sh lets any reader obtain byte-identical images and
verify them, which is what actually matters for reproducing a result.
'expected' hashes marked null are pinned on first successful fetch; see
firmware/MANIFEST.json for the recorded values and fetch timestamps.

device.soc_expected: Realtek RTL8196x (to be confirmed empirically - see notes/anatomy-n150rt.md)

why: Predates the December 2019 Realtek-SDK disclosure by four years.
Expected to contain the vulnerable code paths in their original form,
which makes it the reference point for root-cause analysis.

sources.note: Internet Archive item TOTOLINKN150RTV2.1.2B20150825.1601; hashes below come from the item metadata API, so they are verifiable independently of the download.

notes: The r6cr section header declares a payload length that runs 9 bytes
past the end of this file. Either the archived copy is slightly
truncated or the length field covers a trailer this copy lacks.
Extraction is unaffected - the SquashFS image itself is complete and
unpacks cleanly - but a second source should be compared before the
container format is documented as final.

why: Built 2020-10-30, i.e. nine months AFTER the 2020-01-23 full disclosure
The advisory lists 'N150RT through 3.4.0' as affected, so this build sits
exactly on the boundary. Diffing it against 2.1.2 answers a question the
CVE records do not: did the vendor actually remove the config.dat dump and
the formSysCmd handler, or only the syscmd.htm UI page that exposed it?

sources.note: Third-party firmware mirror. No publisher-supplied hash available; sha256 is pinned on first fetch and any later change is treated as a supply-chain signal, not a silent update.

notes: Pinned on first fetch 2026-08-07 from the only mirror found carrying
this build. No publisher-supplied hash exists to check it against, so
these values assert continuity, not authenticity: if the mirror serves
different bytes later, that is a signal to investigate rather than a

wanted.note: Additional V2-line builds (2.1.1 / 2.1.3 / 2.1.6) are listed on Softpedia but sit behind an interstitial that blocks scripted fetch. The device's own flash dump (W02) is the authoritative image for whatever build this unit actually shipped with, so these are nice-to-have rather than blocking.
